speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're feeling unwell with fatigue, fever, and abdominal pain. To better understand your condition, when did these symptoms first start, and have you noticed any changes in your stool or urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 47-year-old female. The patient describes a 3-week history of generalized fatigue, mild fever, abdominal pain, and nausea. She recalls attending the state fair over a month ago where she tried various regional foods. Recently, she has observed the darkening of her urine, which she believes is due to inadequate water intake. She has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given the dark urine and recent exposure to potential contaminants at the fair, have you experienced any jaundice, clay-colored stools, or severe right upper quadrant pain? Also, has anyone else at the fair become ill?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and mild fever. I also have Abdominal pain, Nausea, Dark urine.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Viral Hepatitis A. The combination of a 3-week history of fatigue, fever, abdominal pain, nausea, and dark urine in a patient with potential fair-ground exposure is highly suggestive of acute viral hepatitis. I will request liver function tests and serology to confirm. REQUEST TEST: LFT Panel, Hepatitis Serology.
